name_reason: Accurately describes behavior: finds a char by char_id (runtime_char +8) with a menu-roster template fallback. Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=find/char query). No Ghidra address residue.
purpose: Find the alive battle character whose char_id == target_char_id (returning its slot index), with a menu-roster template fallback; side-effect caches the matched record pointer for dialog portrait rendering.
logic_summary: __CHK(0x14) stack probe; clear data_fd2_dialog_current_speaker_char_ptr to NULL. Scan runtime_char array [0,party_member_count): on bChar_id(+8)==target_char_id, cache &runtime_char[i] into the global, and if that char is not dead return i immediately. After the battle scan, ONLY if the global is still NULL (no id match at all in battle) scan the menu roster [0,menu_party_member_count) with stride 0x50: on roster[i][+8]==target_char_id, cache that template ptr (last match wins). Always return -1 when no alive battle char was found. A dead battle match caches the runtime_char* and thereby suppresses the fallback while still returning -1.

params.name: param_1
params.semantics: Target character id, matched against runtime_char +8 (bChar_id) and roster template +8. Callers pass ai_aux_byte (= pCombat_aux_block[0xE], the AI's designated target char-id) from fd2_enemy_turn_action_dispatcher cases 3/9, and the dialog speaker char-id from fd2_display_dialog_scene. This is a game-domain character ID, not an address residue.
params.reason: Live Ghidra param is the generic placeholder param_1; src already names it target_char_id. Rename to target_char_id (Stage 2 only) to reflect the matched char_id semantics.

returns.semantics: Slot index of the first alive battle char whose char_id matched; -1 if no alive battle match (including the dead-match and template-fallback cases). The located pointer is also delivered out-of-band via data_fd2_dialog_current_speaker_char_ptr.
